issues.title: Phase number 027 hard-coded in production code and published tool schema (roadmap-isolation violation)
issues.why_it_matters: The developer hard rule is absolute: never reference phase numbers from code or comments, because the codebase must stand alone after roadmap/ is deleted. The constant also embeds a cross-phase coupling into the public wire contract and published schema, and the developer did not escalate the conflict with the phase doc that mandated `honored_from_phase 100270`.
issues.impact: Any renumbering or removal of the roadmap invalidates the value silently; downstream phases 026/027 receive a wire field naming a roadmap artifact rather than a stable capability token.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention.rs:209 `pub const INERT_FIELDS_HONORED_FROM: &str = "027";`; :314 `"honored_from_phase": INERT_FIELDS_HONORED_FROM`; :404 `"x-inert-fields-honored-from"`; :425 and :430 `"honored from phase 100270"`. `./target/debug/am mcp schema-export` output contains "honored from phase 100270" (4 occurrences).
issues.proposed_fix: Replace the phase-number token with a capability token (e.g. `honored_by: "recall_dedup"`) or, if the phase doc's exact `honored_from_phase 100270` field is contractually required, stop and escalate the rule conflict per the developer prompt's requirement-conflict protocol instead of choosing silently.

issues.title: Completion evidence misstates the published schema pack (wrong tool count and mapping keys not actually embedded)
issues.why_it_matters: The phase file is the audit artifact for AC-100250-06. The Completion Evidence claims facts that are demonstrably false, so the acceptance evidence is fudged even though the underlying AC is met.
issues.impact: A reader cannot trust the schema evidence; the mapping tables the phase says are published in the pack are absent from it, which weakens the operator-facing contract the phase promised ('mapping table is published in the schema docs').
issues.evidence: Phase file line 410 claims '`am mcp schema-export` now publishes 41 tools (was 38)' and 'the profile JSON Schema embedded (version stamp `x-retention-profile-version: 1`, `x-verbosity-mapping`, `x-duplicate-tolerance-write-mapping`, `x-theta-offset-bound: 0.20`)'. Actual: `./target/debug/am mcp schema-export` emits 67 tools; raw output contains none of `x-verbosity`, `x-retention`, `x-duplicate`, `x-theta`. `crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_retention_defs.rs:71,97` embed only `profile_json_schema()["properties"]`, dropping the `x-*` metadata and the top-level `additionalProperties`.
issues.proposed_fix: Correct the evidence to the real numbers and either (a) embed the full profile schema (or its x-* mapping keys) in the pack, or (b) restate the evidence as 'mapping tables are published via `am retention schema`, not in the MCP pack'.

issues.title: Hub-distill gated write ignores the bank's resolved retention profile
issues.why_it_matters: Task 1 Required Change 2 requires the resolution function on every gated write. Hub distill is a production, MCP-reachable gated write that still scores with the builtin policy, so a bank set to `selective` gets default strictness for distilled items.
issues.impact: The phase guarantee 'changing a profile controls how strict admission is at write time' does not hold for hub-distilled items; the phase's own monotonicity property is violated on that path.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/hub_distill.rs:199 `let policy = AdmissionPolicy::new(&self.env);` inside `distill_hub`, which calls `gated_create`. HubDistillEngine is built into McpState (crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime.rs:249) and triggered by the bound `consolidate` tool (clio-write/src/memtree_tools.rs:134-190). No retention snapshot is threaded in.
issues.proposed_fix: Thread the resolved `ResolvedRetention` into `HubDistillEngine`/`distill_hub` (or inject a policy factory) so `gated_create` uses `AdmissionPolicy::with_retention`, and add a test that a selective bank rejects a distilled item a balanced bank admits.

issues.title: duplicate_tolerance_write three-level mapping collapses to two values
issues.why_it_matters: The In Scope bullet requires a three-level mapping to the write-side duplicate cutoff; balanced and lenient both resolve to 0.0, so only strict changes behavior. The phase vocabulary also says the two knobs have 'independent defaults and mappings'.
issues.impact: Operators selecting `lenient` get no distinct behavior from `balanced`; the knob is partly decorative on the write path.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention.rs:176-183 `write_novelty_floor()` returns 0.0 for both Balanced and Lenient; mapping table at :39-43; documented as a Known Limitation in the phase file §12.
issues.proposed_fix: Accept the documented limitation as-is (regression constraint) and make the phase doc's In Scope wording say 'three-level enum with strict distinct', or give lenient a distinct (e.g. negative-clamped) value that preserves the existing default behavior.

issues.title: Persistence failure leaves the new profile applied in memory while returning an error
issues.why_it_matters: Negative testing requires that a partial failure does not leave invalid state. On a save error the in-memory store already holds the new profile, so the caller is told the write failed yet a subsequent read returns it.
issues.impact: A failed `retention_profile_set`/CLI set changes admission strictness for the process even though the caller saw an error, and a later successful persist is not required to reconcile.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/config/retention_ops.rs:95-96 (`set_bank` mutates, then `persist_retention()?` may fail); crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_retention.rs:52-58 same pattern. The failure-path test crates/clio-config/src/config/retention_tests.rs:124-141 asserts the error code but never re-reads the store.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate, persist to disk first (or roll back the in-memory insertion on save failure), and extend the failure test to assert the stored profile is unchanged after an I/O error.

issues.title: Span-verify refusals stamp the builtin profile version, not the resolved one
issues.why_it_matters: The phase guarantee says admission decisions always carry the resolved profile_version for audit. These Decision values hard-code the builtin constant.
issues.impact: Currently inert because every profile is version 1, but a future profile version would be misattributed on the verify-refusal path.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs:164 and crates/clio-write/src/store_path.rs:81 both set `profile_version: clio_config::retention::RETENTION_PROFILE_VERSION` rather than the policy's resolved version.
issues.proposed_fix: Pass the resolved profile version (or the AdmissionPolicy) into `refuse_decision`/`verify_reject`.

issues.title: permissive can be set as the deployment default despite 'MUST NOT become a default'
issues.why_it_matters: The phase states `permissive` is intentionally loose and MUST NOT become a default, but nothing prevents `retention_profile_set(scope=deployment, verbosity=permissive)`.
issues.impact: A single deployment-scope write silently loosens admission for every bank without an override.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-config/src/retention.rs:257-286 `validate()` never inspects verbosity; `RetentionStore::set_deployment` (retention_store.rs:115-119) only validates. MCP scope=deployment path at crates/clio-mcp/src/retention_tools.rs:102-106.
issues.proposed_fix: Reject `permissive` for `scope=deployment` (or require an explicit override flag), and add a test.

findings.title: duplicate_tolerance_write three-level mapping collapses to two values
findings.recommendation: Accept as documented limitation with explicit scope wording, or give lenient a distinct behavior.

resolution.status: Resolved by documented limitation (no code change)
resolution.note: The write-side mapping is three-level with `strict` distinct (0.25); `balanced`/`lenient` share the 0.0 floor because the regression constraint forbids changing default admission. A distinct `lenient` value cannot exist without either a meaningless negative novelty floor or changing prior behavior; the phase file §12 limitation already states what is missing, why, and the owning phase. Phase-file remediation note added.

findings.title: Persistence failure leaves the new profile applied in memory while returning an error

findings.recommendation: Roll back the in-memory insertion on save failure, or persist before mutating, and assert it in a test.

resolution.note: Both write paths now roll back on persist failure: `Runtime::retention_profile_set`/`_set_deployment` restore the previous bank override / deployment before returning the I/O error (crates/clio-config/src/config/retention_ops.rs), and `McpState::set_retention`/`set_retention_deployment` do the same under one lock (crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime_retention.rs). Failure tests extended to re-read the store: config `retention_profile_errors_and_in_memory_only_paths` asserts source stays builtin; new `runtime_retention_tests::failed_persist_rolls_back_the_in_memory_store` covers both bank and deployment scopes; `successful_persist_keeps_the_stored_change` covers the success arm.

strengths: Clean separation: clio-config owns the profile/store, clio-admission stays I/O-free and consumes a Copy snapshot, clio-mcp binds tools and publishes schema.
Monotonicity is proven at both unit level (decision_tests) and integration level (T100250-01), including subset (not just count) checks.
Batch preview reuses the exact single-item scoring path and is proven write-free by a store diff and a direct id lookup.
Failure modes are well covered: invalid enum, unknown offset key, oversize offset, NaN/Inf, oversize/empty batch, per-item error, corrupt store, unwritable path.
Transport parity is tested end to end for the new tools rather than asserted.
The store_write.rs extraction kept write_tools.rs under the 450-line cap and the gate-boundary allowlist was updated honestly.
Known limitations are disclosed with cause and owner instead of hidden.
regrets: The developer chose the phase doc's phase-number field over the explicit hard rule without escalating, which is exactly the requirement-conflict case the prompt says to stop on.
The completion evidence paragraph appears to have been written from expectation (mapping tables in the pack, 41 tools) rather than re-read from the actual schema-export output.
process_changes: Any evidence block quoting a command's output should paste the real output; the schema-pack paragraph would have failed a copy-paste check.
When a phase doc and a hard rule conflict (phase numbers in code), stop and signal a blocker with two options instead of silently picking one.

options.name: B: approved exception

pros: No public contract change; downstream phases keep the field the doc pinned

cons: The no-phase-numbers hard rule loses its absolute character and needs an exception mechanism that does not exist
